Do you have a strong interest in using artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques in chemical engineering to create a safer and more sustainable work environment in the oil, gas, petrochemical and chemical industries?

Do you want to further your career through a project with one of the UK’s leading research-intensive universities whilst pursuing a career in industry?

We are seeking an Engineer in Machine Learning or Computational Modelling for a Knowledge Transfer Partnership (KTP) Associate position based at ioMosaic International Ltd in Bath.

About the role

This Knowledge Transfer Partnership will bring together an exciting combination of expertise in artificial intelligence and chemical engineering to deliver a new tool for decision-making in process safety engineering. The tool will deliver a step-change in the design of processing plants, improving safety and reducing environmental impact. 

You will work within ioMosaic Corporation to embed knowledge through this innovation project, with research and academic support from the University. 

This is an opportunity for you to ‘fast track’ your career into business by leading a high profile and strategically meaningful project to a successful conclusion, allowing you to utilise your academic achievements in an industrial setting. 

By joining this KTP between ioMosaic Corporation and the Departments of Chemical Engineering and Computer Science at the University of Bath you will have the opportunity to work on challenges, using ground-breaking technology with incredible team support and development opportunities. 

ioMosaic Corporation is a rapidly growing company providing consulting services in the areas of process safety and risk management in the oil, gas, petrochemical and chemical industries. Based at ioMosaic in Bath, you will be a member of a wider multidisciplinary team, as well as working with the software project team in the UK and US. 

The ideal candidate will have:

A Masters or PhD level qualification in Chemical or Mechanical Engineering.
Experience or strong interest in programming, modelling, or simulation (e.g. Python, MATLAB, C++, or similar platforms).
Familiarity with numerical or simulation tools such as ANSYS, ASPEN, COMSOL, or OpenFOAM. 
Proven skills in AI and machine learning.

You will play a major role in the KTP and engage with multiple stakeholders, so must have excellent communication and organisational skills.

About KTPs

As a KTP Associate you will be the project lead, managing your own workload to ensure outputs align with project expectations, including leading on meetings. You will also acquire new skills in strategic leadership that can help to super-charge your career.

Additional benefits of being a KTP Associate:

All KTP Associates spend 10% of their time on Personal Development, making full use of a generous £2,000 annual personal development budget.
Access to two 1-week residential training sessions at Ashorne Hill, aimed at developing project management skills.
Potential to fast-track a career into business, with an opportunity to gain a permanent job following the KTP. 
Access to a wealth of academic and industrial resources.
Access to a Travel & Subsistence budget.
Access to mentoring and coaching sessions through Innovate UK Business Connect.

It is essential that you understand how KTP works with business and the University, and the vital role you will play.

Further information

As a KTP Associate you can enjoy the benefits of being an employee at the University of Bath whilst working full-time at ioMosaic. 

This is a full-time in-office role based at the company offices in Bath and the University of Bath.

You will be entitled to 25 days paid annual leave in addition to UK public holidays. Working hours are 8:45am to 5:30pm Monday to Friday.

This is a fixed-term role for a period of 29 months.

For any questions about this role please email partnerships@bath.ac.uk

There will be a two stage interview process: an initial online screening and an in-person interview at the ioMosaic office in Bath, in January 2027.

We consider ourselves to be a university where difference is celebrated, respected and encouraged. We have an excellent international reputation with staff from over 60 different nations and have made a positive commitment towards gender equity and intersectionality receiving a Silver Athena SWAN award. We truly believe that diversity of experience, perspectives, and backgrounds will lead to a better environment for our employees and students and encourage applications from all genders, backgrounds, and communities, particularly from under-represented groups, and value the positive impact that will have on the university. We are committed to maintaining a safe and secure environment for our students, staff, and community by reinforcing our Safer Recruitment commitment.

We're very proud to be a signatory of the Armed Forces Covenant. an accredited Disability Confident Leader; autism friendly university, committed to building disability confidence and supporting disabled staff. 

What we can offer you 

We're continually expanding our benefits package to better support you and enhance your experience with us and the below is just an example of some of the many great benefits we offer:

Generous employer contributory pension schemes
Cycle to work scheme
Electric vehicle salary sacrifice scheme
Staff discount at Team Bath gym
Staff benefits include discounted postgraduate tuition and language courses, alongside a wide range of personal and professional development opportunities such as apprenticeships, LinkedIn Learning, and more
Local discounts, including free entry to the Holburne Museum in Bath
Relocation allowance
Visa reimbursement and Interest-Free Loan to help with the cost of some immigration expenses
Employee assistance services through Health Assured, including access to the Wisdom app

Find out more about our benefits and watch the video to hear from our staff about what makes the University of Bath a great place to work as well as following us on X and LinkedIn.

Be Well at Bath

We’re committed to creating a health-supporting working environment where everyone can thrive and be at their best. We offer a range of resources to enable you to do that from your first day here, including:

Staff support groups and networks
A network of Staff Wellbeing Champions
A suite of tools, resources and frameworks that enable you to be at your best and thrive

Find out more about being at your best at Bath.

 Location:  Life and Mind Building, South Parks Road, Oxford OX1 3EL 

 We are seeking a Senior Postdoctoral Research Scientist to join the Kraemer Group in the Data Analytics and Epidemiology (DAE) group at the Pandemic Sciences Institute (PSI), University of Oxford. Working with Professor Moritz Kraemer and Dr Cathal Mills, you will help lead the development of a global, real-time, probabilistic forecasting observatory for climate-sensitive infectious diseases, including dengue, cholera, and malaria. 

 You will develop, implement, and validate spatiotemporal mathematical, statistical, and machine learning models for disease risk mapping, forecasting, and scenario modelling. You will integrate large-scale datasets across epidemiological, environmental, climatic, demographic, genomic, and behavioural modalities, evaluate probabilistic forecasts, maintain a public-facing forecasting dashboard, and work with international public health partners globally to support local model adoption through co-design workshops and training. 

 You will hold a PhD/DPhil with post-qualification research experience in a relevant quantitative discipline (such as epidemiology, computer science, mathematics, statistics, or computational biology). You will have demonstrable experience modelling climate-sensitive infectious diseases, developing and deploying forecasting and scenario models, and building reproducible analytical workflows in Python, R, Julia, and/or other relevant programming languages. Strong analytical, communication, organisational, and collaborative skills are essential. 

 The University of Oxford is committed to equality and valuing diversity. All applicants will be judged on merit, according to the selection criteria. 

 This post is full-time on a fixed-term contract until 31st January 2028, funded by the Medical Research Foundation (MRF), and available immediately. 

 Applications for this vacancy should be made online via our e-recruitment system, and you will be required to upload a supporting statement and CV as part of your online application (via the ' Apply ' button above). Your supporting statement must explain how you meet each of the selection criteria for the post using examples of your skills and experience. Please restrict your documentation to your CV and supporting statement only. Any other documents will be requested at a later date. The deadline for applications is 12:00 noon on Monday 23 November 2026 .

 Location: Pandemic Sciences Institute, Li Ka Shing Centre for Health and Information Discovery, Old Road Campus, Headington, Oxford, OX3 7LF

 We are seeking to appoint a Research Fellow in Outbreak Response to join the Data Analytics and Epidemiology group at the Pandemic Sciences Institute, Nuffield Department of Medicine. Working with Professor Moritz Kraemer, you will contribute to B-REACT, a project funded by the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI), supporting the response to the Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). The research will focus on developing real-time spatial models of infectious disease transmission to inform outbreak response, surveillance, vaccine research and clinical trial preparedness.

 You will be responsible for developing and running real time spatial and metapopulation models of disease transmission, integrating epidemiological, mobility, genomic and geospatial data to forecast outbreak risks and support public health decision-making. The role includes developing reproducible analytical pipelines, producing forecasts and surveillance assessments, communicating findings to policymakers and collaborating with international research partners. You will also lead research activities, contribute to publications, manage resources and support capacity building and technology transfer with national public health teams in the DRC.

 It is essential that you hold a relevant PhD/DPhil with post-qualification research experience in epidemiology, statistics, mathematics, computational biology or a related quantitative discipline. You should have experience developing spatial or metapopulation models of infectious disease transmission, model evaluation and uncertainty quantification, alongside strong Python and/or R programming skills and experience analysing large-scale, real-world datasets. Excellent communication, organisational and project management skills, a strong publication record, grant-writing ability and experience working collaboratively across international research teams are required. Experience in phylogenetic or phylodynamic methods, outbreak response in low- and middle-income countries, developing dashboards or visualisations, vaccine trial analytics, or a working knowledge of French would be advantageous.

 Applications for this vacancy should be made online (via the ' Apply ' button above) and you will need to upload a supporting statement and CV. Your supporting statement must explain how you meet each of the selection criteria for the post using examples of your skills and experience. Please restrict your documentation to your CV and supporting statement only. Any other documents will be requested at a later date.

 This position is offered full time on a fixed term contract for 12 months and is funded by the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI).

 Only applications received before 12 midday on 6 November 2026 will be considered. Please quote 189423 on all correspondence.

 The post may also be offered as a secondment opportunity.

 About the job: 

 We are seeking an outstanding researcher to contribute to the HARMONICA project, an EU Horizon-funded Research and Innovation Action advancing Europe's recycling sector towards a human-centric Industry 5.0 model. The post will focus on adaptive human-robot teaming: developing intelligent systems that understand a human team member's changing cognitive and physical state and dynamically adapt robot behaviour and autonomy in complex shopfloor environments.

 The successful candidate will work at the intersection of Human-Robot Interaction (HRI), human-centred AI, multimodal sensing and machine learning, developing real-time approaches that enable robots and semi-autonomous mobile manipulators to respond appropriately to human workload, attention, capability and performance.

 About the person: 

 The successful candidate must have and your application should clearly demonstrate that you meet the following essential criteria: 

 Have or be about to obtain a PhD in a relevant area such as: Human-Computer Interaction, Human-Robot Interaction, Artificial Intelligence / Machine Learning, Human Factors / Cognitive Systems, Computer Science or a closely related discipline.

 Significant, recent, relevant experience to include: 
 Human participant experimental design

 Human cognitive/workload modelling

 Multimodal sensing and data fusion

 Time-series or real-time data analysis

 Human-Robot Interaction

 Adaptive or shared autonomy

 Human factors and experimental evaluation

 Real-time intelligent systems

 Demonstrable experience in programming/scripting, beyond that taught in undergraduate engineering courses.

 A proven track record of using relevant techniques to carry out analyses, critical evaluations, and interpretations of data in a research context.

 This is not an exhaustive list. To be successful at shortlisting stage, please ensure you clearly evidence in your application how you meet the essential and, where applicable, desirable criteria listed in the Candidate Brief on our website.

Job Title:  Research Associate in Biomaterials and Implant Immunology
Posting Start Date:  02/11/2026
Job Id:  3355
School/Department:  Chemical, Materials & Biological Engineering
Work Arrangement:  Full Time (On site)
Contract Type:  Fixed-term
Salary per annum (£):  39,560 - 41,885
Closing Date:  15/11/2026

The University of Sheffield is a remarkable place to work. Our people are at the heart of everything we do. Their diverse backgrounds, abilities and beliefs make Sheffield a world-class university.

We offer a fantastic range of benefits including a highly competitive annual leave entitlement (with the ability to purchase more), a generous pensions scheme, flexible working opportunities, a commitment to your development and wellbeing, a wide range of retail discounts, and much more. Find out more about our benefits (opens in a new window) and join us to become part of something special.

 

Overview

 

Are you completing, or have you completed, a PhD in biomaterials, tissue engineering, cell biology, regenerative medicine or a related area, with an interest in improving the safety of implantable medical devices? We have an exciting opportunity to join a research programme establishing a coordinated framework for the analysis of explanted polymeric medical devices.

 

You will contribute to research investigating how implant degradation, tissue responses and patient-specific factors combine to drive complications associated with specific medical devices. You will help establish robust experimental and sample-handling workflows for explanted devices and matched biological samples, develop and establish laboratory methods to characterise tissue and immune responses, and support the integration of research findings within a developing explant research programme.

 

Working within the School of Chemical, Materials and Biological Engineering, you will collaborate with academic, clinical, regulatory and patient partners, including Sheffield Teaching Hospitals and the University of Cambridge. You will contribute to publications, presentations and project outputs with direct relevance to patient safety and post-market device surveillance.

 

This role offers an excellent opportunity to develop multidisciplinary expertise at the interface of biomaterials, implant immunology, women’s health and translational healthcare research, while contributing to a programme designed to deliver lasting clinical and regulatory impact.

 

Main duties and responsibilities

 

Contribute to the delivery of the research programme investigating the causes and consequences of failure of polymeric implantable medical devices, with a particular focus on implant-tissue and immune interactions.
Develop, optimise and document experimental and sample-handling workflows for explanted medical devices and matched biological samples, including periprosthetic tissues and, where available, peri-implant aspirates.
Undertake laboratory-based research using relevant cell and tissue models, including mammalian cell culture and human tissue-based approaches, to investigate biological responses to implant materials and degradation products.
Develop and apply appropriate methods for characterising tissue and immune responses, which may include histological assessment, immunostaining, microscopy and relevant cellular or molecular assays.
Support the integration of experimental findings with implant characterisation and patient-level clinical information within the developing explant registry, working closely with the Principal Investigator (Dr Nicholas Farr) and project collaborators.
Analyse, interpret and quality-assure experimental data, maintaining accurate, reproducible research records and contributing to the development of standard operating procedures and research protocols.
Work collaboratively with academic, clinical and regulatory partners.
Contribute to the preparation of high-quality research outputs, including peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, reports and materials for clinical, regulatory and public audiences.
Ensure research is conducted in accordance with relevant ethical, health and safety, human tissue, data protection and research governance requirements, and contribute to appropriate documentation and approvals.
Support the wider activities of the research group, including sharing expertise, contributing to the training or supervision of students and researchers where appropriate, and supporting an inclusive and collaborative research environment.
Carry out other duties, commensurate with the grade and remit of the post.

 

Person Specification

Our diverse community of staff and students recognises the unique abilities, backgrounds, and beliefs of all. We foster a culture where everyone feels they belong and is respected. Even if your past experience doesn't match perfectly with this role's criteria, your contribution is valuable, and we encourage you to apply. Please ensure that you reference the application criteria in the application statement when you apply.

Proud to be Sunderland 

The University of Sunderland offers life‑changing opportunities for more than 27,500 students across our campuses in Sunderland, London and Hong Kong, as well as through global partnerships in 19 countries. 

We’re an inclusive, ambitious and forward‑looking University in a vibrant city that’s constantly evolving. We’re also entering an exciting new phase with a refreshed vision and strategic ambitions shaped around the changing higher education landscape.

As we move through 2026, we’re celebrating being recognised as: 

A top 30 UK university (Guardian University Guide 2026)
1st in the North‑East for student support services (Daily Mail University Guide 2026)

Your next opportunity

Help build the future of AI-enabled healthcare.

The Northern Ophthalmic Research and Innovation (NORI) Institute is an ambitious partnership between the Universities of Sunderland, Durham, and Newcastle, South Tyneside and Sunderland NHS Foundation Trust, and a network of national and international partners. Our mission is to transform how health and disease are detected, understood, and managed through the integration of advanced analytics, multimodal health data, retinal imaging, artificial intelligence, and real-world clinical innovation.

We are seeking an exceptional Principal Research Fellow to play a leading role in designing and delivering the health data intelligence that underpins this vision. This is a rare opportunity to help shape a nationally significant research platform from the ground up that supports cutting-edge research and the deployment of data-driven technologies into healthcare.

Working across university, NHS, civic, and industry partners, you will lead research using medical imaging, electronic health records and clinical text. You will collaborate with academic, NHS and industry partners, shape the data and analytical infrastructure supporting your research, and develop new funding opportunities.

This is an externally funded 4-year fixed term contract.

Is this you?

The successful candidate will have – 

1. A relevant PhD and a strong record of original, peer-reviewed healthcare machine learning research, with advanced expertise in developing and rigorously validating explainable, robust AI methods using clinical text, images or structured health records.

2. Experience leading multidisciplinary research projects or substantial work packages with NHS, academic or industry partners, delivering agreed outputs, managing resources and risks, contributing substantively to successful external funding applications, and supervising or mentoring researchers.

3. Experience translating research priorities into secure data and analytical infrastructure requirements, coordinating delivery with specialist technical colleagues, and applying sound judgement on research ethics, information governance and responsible AI when working with sensitive health data.

Why join us?

At the University of Sunderland, we’re more than a place of learning, we’re a welcoming community that values inclusivity, collaboration, and well-being. We don’t just offer jobs, we offer careers that come with support, flexibility, and plenty of perks: 

Up to 49 days’ holiday - that’s 36 days’ annual leave, 5 festive closure days and 8 Bank Holidays! 
Award-winning staff networks that celebrate who you are. 
Lifestyle benefits, with savings on shopping, tech, bikes, and even cars. 
Health and well-being support, from private medical cover to gym discounts. 
Learning and development that helps you achieve your goals.

Ready to Apply?

Before getting started, please download the Role Profile under ‘Job Description’ so you have everything you need. 

Our application questions assess you directly against the essential and desirable criteria for the role. We do not review CVs at this stage, so please provide detailed, evidence-based answers to help us understand your suitability. 

Closing date: Monday 9th November (23:59 GMT)

If you have questions about the role, please contact:

NORI Director, Matthew Campbell: matthew.campbell@sunderland.ac.uk 

We may close this vacancy earlier than the advertised closing date if we receive a high volume of applications. If this sounds like the opportunity for you, don't wait – get your application in early!

We are seeking a motivated Research Assistant to deliver the preclinical work package of an interdisciplinary programme investigating the cardiac effects of clozapine and whether co-administration of tirzepatide can prevent or reverse cardiac dysfunction.

Assistant Research Manager
Requisition ID:  29871
Location:  

Newcastle, GB

Contract Type:  Open Ended
Working Pattern:  Full Time
Posted Date:  2 Nov 2026

Salary: £37,369.00 - £46,970.00  per annum

 

Newcastle University is a great place to work, with excellent benefits. We have a generous holiday package; plus the opportunity to buy more, great pension schemes and a number of health and wellbeing initiatives to support you.

 

Closing Date: 23 November 2026

 

The Role

 

Newcastle University is seeking a people oriented and proactive professional to join the Faculty of Science, Agriculture and Engineering (SAgE) as an Assistant Research Manager.

 

This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in managing and implementing research service delivery in a dynamic research environment.

 

You will work closely with the School Research Manager to provide robust, agile and coordinated research proposal support for an allocated unit in the SAgE Faculty. You will support in the delivery of key strategic initiatives aligned to unit, Faculty and University priorities.

 

To carry out this role you will take the lead on development and implementation of research proposal strategy and support for the unit, developing and managing key relationships with a range of stakeholders.

 

You will be a dedicated strong team player who is comfortable in taking the lead whilst working in a matrix structure. You will be a proactive problem solver, with the ability to negotiate and influence colleagues across organisational boundaries.

 

You will report directly to the School Research Manager, deputising when required and supporting areas of research management and service delivery in line with strategic priority need.

 

The role is offered on a full-time basis. We would welcome requests for flexible working and depending on the needs of the role, blended working opportunities to work remotely as well as on campus may be considered. The hiring manager will discuss the requirements of the role, should you be invited to interview.

 

For informal enquiries about the role please contact Lizzie Bell, School Research Manager for Computing and Mathematics, Statistics and Physics, (Elizabeth.Bell2@newcastle.ac.uk).

 

To apply, please attach your CV and a cover letter that demonstrates how you meet the essential criteria for the position, as outlined in the Person Specification of the Job Description. Any requested additional documents required as part of your application, should be included within the same file as your cover letter. The total file size must not exceed 10MB.

 

Key Accountabilities

Working closely with the School Research Manager to develop and implement a strategic plan for awareness and support of all research proposals across the unit
To coordinate and provide agile and visible PS support for all research proposals across the unit, bringing in specialist teams from across the University (for example, Research Funding and Development and Newcastle Innovations)
To provide sound advice and guidance relating to all areas of costings, costing and pricing strategies and actively support in costing proposals. Where appropriate, work closely with and line manage the Research Proposal Officer allocated to a unit to ensure appropriate and fully maximised costing of applications
To identify and implement mechanisms that support a thriving, inclusive and supportive environment for research proposal development and clear understanding of the proposal pipeline within the unit
To coordinate and ensure appropriate support for the timely submission of high-quality complex funding applications
To ensure knowledge and expertise in advising and signposting for research funding applicants in relation to non-finance support - such as ethics, funder guidelines, data management plans, trusted research
To implement processes and mechanisms to ensure all appropriate teams meet regularly to review proposal applications, and that appropriate involvement and timely advice is provided to PS and academic colleagues
Support the School Research Manager in the implementation of induction and appropriate training and development for research and research-enabling colleagues
Work with the Head of Faculty Research, Finance and other teams, together with Assistant Research Managers to ensure that opportunities to enhance and create a consistent approach to research support are optimised
You will report directly to the School Research Manager, deputising when required and supporting areas of research management and service delivery in line with strategic priority need

 

The Person (Essential)

 

Knowledge, Skills and Experience

A sound understanding and knowledge of the research environment
Experience of research administration either with a funding agency or higher education institution
A demonstrable understanding of how to build a culture of equality, diversity and inclusion
Effective collaboration, influencing and negotiation skills in an environment where resources may not be within their direct control
An ability to recognise and analyse the dynamics of problems and issues and provide innovative solutions
An ability to think strategically and comfortable working at a complex level including the management of conflicting priorities and demands
Experience of costing and managing projects or equivalent experience (Desirable)
Experience of developing and implementing strategy in the research environment, preferably in a HEI or other research focussed organisation (Desirable)

 

Attributes and Behaviour

Acts in a collaborative, inclusive, collegiate, transparent and open manner, acting with integrity and able to build trust with colleagues and partners
An energetic and "can do" approach which will inspire and enthuse others, ready to take the lead in driving forward initiatives
A role model of the University values and guiding principles who promotes a culture of mutual respect
An articulate and confident communicator, able to deal with difficult situations and to challenge where necessary
An exceptional team player confident in working in partnership with others within and outside the organisation
An ability to act objectively in dealing with complex problems, issues and decision making

 

Qualifications

Degree or equivalent level qualification and/or experience in a similar research related role

 

Newcastle University is a global University where everyone is treated with dignity and respect.  As a University of Sanctuary, we aim to provide a welcoming place of safety for all, offering opportunities to people fleeing violence and persecution.

 

We are committed to being a fully inclusive university which actively recruits, supports and retains colleagues from all sectors of society.  We value diversity as well as celebrate, support and thrive on the contributions of all of our employees and the communities they represent.  We are proud to be an equal opportunities employer and encourage applications from individuals who can complement our existing teams, we believe that success is built on having teams whose backgrounds and experiences reflect the diversity of our university and student population.

 

At Newcastle University we hold a Gold Athena Swan award in recognition of our good employment practices for the advancement of gender equality.  We also hold a Race Equality Charter Bronze award in recognition of our work towards tackling race inequality in higher education REC.  We are a Disability Confident employer and will offer an interview to disabled applicants who meet the essential criteria for the role as part of the offer and interview scheme.

 

In addition, we are a member of the Euraxess initiative supporting researchers in Europe.

 About the role – We invite applications for a Research Assistant to join our team on an  EDI Hub+ funded project which aims to address systemic barriers in the way that reasonable adjustments are implemented, specifically for neurodivergent postgraduate researchers. The role will involve planning and conducting research activities, including surveys and focus groups, and liaising with stakeholder groups to co-develop materials and resources. With this project we want to co-create a set of resources that will support students and supervisors to identify appropriate reasonable adjustments, including practical guidance that will improve inclusive practice at Higher Education Institutions.

 About the team-  You will be working in the School of Psychology with Dr Lauren Marsh. You will also collaborate with team members from other departments and universities:  Dr Claudia Matz – Doctoral Training Centre, University of Nottingham and Prof Manda Banerji – Astrophysics at the University of Southampton. The project involves co-creation with multiple stakeholder groups, including neurodivergent postgraduate researchers, postgraduate research supervisors, and disability support teams.

 About you-  You should have knowledge or experience of neurodiversity, and analysing qualitative or quantitative research data. Additionally, you should have developing research skills in Psychology or a related discipline, as evidenced by an undergraduate degree, or equivalent experience. Experience with co-design methodologies would be beneficial.

 What we offer-  

 A friendly, diverse, and supportive working environment

 A hybrid working arrangement with the blended approach of home and office working each week

 Generous holiday entitlement of 30 days (or pro rata) plus standard bank holidays and five university closure days including closure between Christmas and New Year.

 Our reward scheme grants bonuses of numerous values for excellent work

 We are committed to staff development through the provision of training, continued support, and career progression opportunities

 You will have access to a range of benefits and rewards, including fitness and health facilities, staff discounts, travel schemes and many more. To find out more about what we can offer you, follow the link to our benefits website 

 What next-  The post will be offered on a part-time basis (29 hours per week, fixed term contract), with an expected start date of 25 th January 2027 to 17 th December 2027 (approximately 11 months). A later start may be considered, subject to the contract ending no later than 10 January 2028.

 Further information is available in the role profile. To apply for this vacancy please click ‘Apply Now’ to complete your details.

 Please contact (Ellie Ryder Ellie.Faulkner@nottingham.ac.uk ) if you have further questions about this role. Please note that applications sent directly to this email address will not be accepted.

 Please note that should you require a Skilled Worker Visa to undertake this role we are able to sponsor the visa (subject to eligibility) but we will not be able to reimburse any visa expenses (application fees, health surcharge etc.). Interview travel expenses will also not be reimbursed.

 Oxford, Hybrid

 Hours: 
 Part Time 

 Contract Type: 
 Fixed-Term/Contract 

 Placed On: 
 2nd November 2026 

 Closes: 
 19th November 2026 

 Job Ref: 
 189382 

 Location Department of Social Policy and Intervention, 32 Wellington Square, Oxford, OX1 2ER

 About the role  

 The Department of Social Policy and Intervention is seeking a part-time Research Assistant to provide research and project coordination support for a John Fell Fund funded project examining how secondary schools make decisions about the adoption and use of digital mental health tools. 

 The successful candidate will contribute to a range of research activities, with a particular focus on qualitative data collection and analysis. This will include school visits, interviews with key stakeholders, and supporting the delivery of a participatory workshop with young people. 

 The role is fixed term until 9 April 2027. 

 About you  

 You will hold a first degree in psychology, education, or a related field, together with some relevant experience. You will have knowledge of social science research methods and experience of qualitative data collection and analysis. Able to manage your own research and administrative activities effectively, you will possess excellent communication skills, including the ability to produce high quality written outputs, present findings to a range of audiences, and represent the research team at meetings. You will have experience of working collaboratively within a team, along with the ability to follow, adapt, and apply research methodologies as required. 

 Experience of working with schools and/or adolescents would be advantageous, as would experience of case study development and contributing to academic publications.

 You will be based in Oxford as your normal place of work however there is opportunity for remote working, as agreed with the manager. 

 The Department of Social Policy and Intervention holds a Bronze Athena Swan Award which demonstrates our commitment towards advancement of gender equality in higher education and research institutions: equal opportunities, representation and success for all. 

 How to apply  

 As part of your application you will be required to upload a  CV  and  supporting statement , along with the name and contact details of two referees. The supporting statement should explain how you meet each of the essential selection criteria for the post using clear examples. This may include experience and skills gained in employment, education or during career breaks (such as time out for dependents).  Please DO NOT attach any other documents to your application as these will not be considered.  

 Further information, including how to apply, is available in the job description (via the ' Apply ' button above). Any further enquires may be directed to the email address hrteam@spi.ox.ac.uk .

 Only online applications received by 12.00 noon on 19 November 2026 will be considered. Interviews will be held week commencing 7 December 2026.
